title: Write-Back Dirty Bit Management
constraints: 8 cache lines, each with a valid and a dirty bit (outputs `valid[i]`, `dirty[i]`). Reset clears both, and also `writeback` and `wb_index`.
`op` on each rising edge: 00 idle, 01 **write** (line becomes valid + dirty), 10 **fill** (new line from memory: valid, clean), 11 **invalidate** (line becomes invalid + clean).
Fill and invalidate evict the old line: if it was valid **and** dirty, pulse `writeback = 1` for one cycle with `wb_index = index`. Otherwise `writeback = 0`.
`wb_index` holds its value when there is no writeback. Must be synthesizable.
hints: Two 8-bit registers plus a registered writeback pulse.
Check the *old* dirty/valid bits (before the update) to decide on the writeback.
A write to an invalid line is a write-allocate hit here: it becomes valid and dirty.

examples.check: fill of a dirty line writes back
examples.title: eviction
examples.input: line 3 dirty, then op = fill, index = 3
